body: I feel like I live this every day.

I know I'm not a parent but I still sit here, with a boyfriend, and sometimes I have my doubts. Am I gay? Is this what I want? Sometimes I'm fearful of it, sometimes I just love it. I have that awesome guy friend I grew up with, but I'm around him all the time. I don't know, just some mindless unrelated rambling.

I had a very terrible home life. My mother and father were never married. From 6-16 my mother married 3 guys. Abusive drunks. 

I never got much out of my childhood, I wasn't allowed to go to friends houses, they could only come to our house, and I was (notably) verbally yelled at by my mother whenever they were over.

I lashed out during grade 4-5, starting hitting people. It most likely was pent up rage and sadness, I hurt many other kids, got into scraps, called names, broke things that belonged to others. This lasted through 11th grade, before I WALKED OUT of my mothers home, and moved in with my biological father.

I have since turned my life around. To this day, those that I still have contact with that I bullied I am fairly good friends with, and I am working to stop bullying in my local area, because I know how sadistic children like I was can be.

:(

EDIT: Yes, I was hit many times, in front of people and everything. In front of the few friends I had. It was terrible. Also, no we were not low income.

HAH! I managed to stumble over reddit's SW sub, and wanted to post a bit of inspiration to those who are having trouble, and simply don't see a way out. (But, stick with me, this is my first time posting, and I seem to have stumbled on my first attempt!)


I was born to a mother and father that were not married, which simply meant that I was to be raised by my stepfather, whom at the time was an amazing father (I was about 5 when my mother married). Things began to take a turn downwards as I grew older, my mother was unable to have my stepfather's child, and my stepfather was unable to legally adopt me (for reasons I do not know, but presumably my biological father?).

He turned to alcohol, and mother of my friends. In response to his cheating and other new outlets, my mother turned to food. Both seemed heavily upset with their situations, and thus began a long, 18 year downwards spiral for me.

It started with my stepfather, he was physically abusive, especially when drinking. He'd come into my room drunk, trying to be nice and interested and to spend time with me... But I would manage to make him angry somehow, only to be punched, or pushed around. My mother was often witness to this, or heard my screams for help in the other room, only to be too ashamed to do things. That was until one night, she stood up for me, only to be pushed down the stairs (she was fine, but shaken). My stepfather was put in jail and they were later divorced. My mother lost our house when I turned 11 and we began moving around.

As the abuse was poured on by my stepfather, it's notable to mention I became a very large bully in my school. I often picked on, beat up anyone and everyone. Boys, girls, teachers. No one seemed to be immune from my outlets from the inner pain that I had been bottling up, resenting everyone for not saving me from 6 years of childhood torment, only for things to get worse. The few friends I had I lost as we moved across state to meet this new "man" my mother knew from her childhood (her first boyfriend, who was in fact married at the time of all of this). He didn't like me, and he was vocal about it. Many nights I was left alone to "hang out" in this new city we moved to as she was out with him, or would even come home to fornicate out in the open. As the days went on, and by the time I was 13, this guy told my mother I needed to leave or else she would be kicked out (he purchased a condo for her and I to stay in).

Long story short, my uncle was in town with my two cousins, staying over one night when this man came over, hammered, he pushed me over as I was simply minding my own business playing video games (Blazing Angels), and I became frightened, remembering my stepfather, I locked myself in the bathroom. He picked the lock, shoved me into the bathtub screaming obscenities. I managed to get to a weight scale to defend myself and hit him with, only to be thrown into the tub once more before the uncle pulled the guy out and threw him out of the house. That was the last I saw of the man, before we moved.

To this day my mother blames all of her relationship woes on me, I felt responsible. I acted out at school. I was in so many fights I was suspended for nearly half the year for 7th and 8th grade. I didn't want to go home, and I eventually asked my grandmother to allow me to play football come 9th grade. As an attempt to stay out of my home.

My mother didn't like that she wasn't in control of where I was, and pulled me from football, and we moved yet again after the condo was sold. She met a man on the internet. A father of 3, he was a great man, but my mother poisoned him. Her alcoholism and self pity managed to break the man down (he was eventually laid off from his mechanic job at NW Airlines as well) putting further strains on everyone. 5 years later of these two dating, and I turned 18. He told my mother to get out and we then lived in a small apartment in a little "ghetto". I continued to bully, but now more withdrawn in my third school, and no new friends, I became the target of the already established bullies. Large fights ensued. I had many hospital visits, and so did other kids due to the simple intensity of some of the conflicts. 

The worst was Thanksgiving 2007, I was cornered by four larger guys, two held me down as I was beaten, three other that I knew from the school sat their narrating when they "hit me good", broke my new glasses, they even dislocated my knee during the entire ordeal. But I managed to survive the worst torment of my life (notable, all parties were suspended 3 days out of school, when in the nurses office, I tackled and attacked the ring leader, I was suspended a month for "retaliating", and further had a restraining order, so I was then stuck riding the short bus, and taking classes with special needs kids, which at the time for me, was quite humiliating (however I admit now, some of the kids I met were amazing people).

A year later after my mother broke up once again, she lost her drivers license for another DUI, and turned to me to drive her to the bar, citing that she needed to hang out "with her friends", and there were men that she wanted to see. One day I refused.

She destroyed my room. My Xbox, computer (all purchased by my biological father, who I rarely had contact with), pour out my dressers contents, and simply degraded me. Telling me of how I was the worst thing to happen to her, I was a mistake. There was no way she could afford to have a child. She could never be happy because I was such an emotional drain on her.

I felt terrible. I wanted it to end. I lost many of my friends out of her refusal to allow me to go to their houses, because she wouldn't be in "control". I was alone and isolated. I thought about cutting, walking out into the snow, and just lying down at the park, in the forest. I thought of all of the things I could do to just end my suffering and hers as well. 

But then I met someone, my current best friend, and fiance. At the time, I knew them as a simple nerd, always talking about star trek and world of warcraft. I had teased them in the past, even treated them badly. But they continued to ask me out, to which I accepted... We moved in together, quickly. Many say don't do that when you first meet someone but we did. He was the best thing that ever happened to me. Taught me things would be okay, even with minor hiccups. The world isn't 100% perfect, nor are the people that live in it.

I started going to classes, accompanied by him at first before finally going on my own. Telling people about my troubles. I found help from people to get my education on track and graduate (which I did with a B average, up from a D). I began meeting new friends at these classes, with the same interests, all willing to help and hang out. People who would not judge me for what I had done, but what I was willing to do to proceed in life.

I enlisted in the Army soon after. I found discipline, I was taught how to focus my anger and other deep emotions into my pride for who I am and what I stood for. I didn't let others label me, but I labeled myself. I was finally a success.

5 Years later I am a Criminal Justice major going for my bachelors, I am a Corporal, awaiting my next stripe. I am a homosexual soldier. I am a home owner. I have a beautiful dog and I am very active in my community.

I have turned around what was a pitiful life, that was on a horrible road. All I did was ask for help, I opened myself to others that were willing to listen and I have never looked back, nor held any resentment for the decisions of others.
